caption:
Your price isn't losing you the job.

Your quote format is.

Hand a customer one number and they have exactly one decision: yes or no. If it feels high, they say no and call the next contractor on the list.

Most home service pros still quote this way, one price, one chance to say no.

Give someone three options instead and something predictable happens. They rarely pick the cheapest or the most expensive. They land in the middle. It's one of the most replicated patterns in pricing research.

Next quote, build three:
Good: the code-minimum repair
Better: the repair plus one real upgrade
Best: full replacement or premium option

Price the middle tier as the one you want picked.

See what it does to your numbers. DM TOOLS

#HomeServiceBusiness #ContractorTips #HVAC #Roofing #ServiceBusinessGrowth
rationale: Carousels lead saves/depth for B2B teaching, and this ships a genuinely unclaimed revenue tactic (tiered good/better/best quoting) grounded in the decoy effect, a well-documented behavioral pricing pattern, distinct from every prior follow-up, CRM, and framework post already shipped.
